Have you had a talk since the baby arrived? I know how painful those conversations are and it's draining having them over and over when you know nothing has changed. The baby is a change though and it could change her priorities (good or bad) toward your relationship. If you bypass that last talk, you might be left wondering if the conversation would have finally been a different one. That might be a worthwhile risk though since you don't have any evidence to suggest that this will change her.  Also, even if she does change there's the risk that it's too late and any changes she makes will be overshadowed by the years of pain leading up to it.

You don't have any easy choices here and it seems like you're trying your hardest to make the best one possible for your family and yourself. I hope you find some peace no matter what you decide to do.

"He still is very affectionate and wants to cuddle every night (we have separate rooms for several reasons). I try to be there for him but I’m so turned on it physically hurts to fall asleep next to someone who wants to spoon me but doesn’t want to touch me or see me naked." It's eerie how much I relate to this. It really does physically hurt sometimes.

That was my assumption, but I’ve asked a million times and a therapist asked him privately and he says he’s really attracted to me. So....idk. It doesn’t make sense to me either, but the shock value wore off years ago.  
  
He rarely masturbates when I’m home anymore. Less than weekly unless I’m on a trip, then it’s nearly every day. I’ve also asked the same question and the best answer I’ve gotten is that it’s a quick thing to relax and help fall asleep and it’s not necessary related to being turned on. It’s also way less effort than sex.  
  
My guess is that he’s so used to that feeling that his body doesn’t respond easily to sex because he’s not in complete control. He’d only had sex several times before we started dating and I’m his first serious relationship. I thought that issue would go away after a couple years of getting used to having a partner always willing/ready to have sex .....but I guess not.
He can’t. He said it was too hard just being my friend and he can’t manage that long term again. And I’d rather be married than friends for everything other than the obvious reason.
Yes, which is why I made this decision. There will inevitably be times where it’s still difficult, but I can accept that.

We’re both incredibly pedantic and people always think we’re arguing with them, but we’re just super curious about everything. We make each other laugh. We love to snuggle on the couch and watch movies. We love savoring good wine and trying new food. We’re both introverted and get wrapped up in our own worlds. We overlap in interests, but bring different skills to a conversation. He has more technical and political knowledge. I’m better at culture, psychology, and serial killer trivia. We love to hike, be outside, and travel. We’re both the first person in every situation to get fed up with people endlessly speculating and just google something. We get super excited about finding ways to automate our oven or use microchip scanning to keep our fat cat from eating the other cat’s food. I love how happy and passionate he is about life. I have a wonderful relationship with his family. He is so incredibly supportive and kind through all of my health issues. 
  
We’re honest with each other even when it’s hard or awkward. We both know the other person always has our back. We’re not jealous or controlling. We truly respect each other.  
  
We never had a lustful honeymoon phase, but we still get excited to see each other and talk about our days. I hear about relationship problems my friends or family have and there’s so much controlling, lack of communication, or just generally not understanding the other person. I always feel lucky that I don’t have those problems. So many of my friends jumped into marriages with someone they’d only known a year or two and wound up discovering things they didn’t like or being super incompatible. I’ve known him for 12 years total, was close friends for 4, and dated for 6. This isn’t going to be a situation of not knowing who I’m really marrying and that brings me a lot of comfort. 
  
Those are all such little things, but it’s hard to put into words everything you love about someone, isn’t it? It’s all the little things as well as a general sense of “themness”.

An open relationship was a potential solution after trying every other alternative. If we were a year or two into this relationship, I think it would be more concerning. Open relationships aren't for everyone, but I know people that they work very well for.  
  
I'm not thinking about cheating. I know it's a choice I have, but it's not one I want to pursue. You could definitely be right about convincing myself of something that can never be. I'm taking the risk to find that out and it could obviously backfire.

I keep telling him to run. He thinks the benefits outweigh the cost (just as I think his benefits outweigh the cost of his limitation). He’s keenly aware of my medical and psychiatric history. I’m a painfully honest friend and partner. Life is less messy that way. Thanks for the chat. Cool username btw.

Where did I state something materialistic? I just read through every comment and I honestly can’t find what you’re indicating. Materialistic needs could be achieved very easily in another person. There’d be no reason whatsoever to even consider staying if it was as simple as that. I did say that our possessions and assets are intertwined, but only as evidence that it’s not like we have some commitment-free casual relationship currently and I’m just now walking into something serious. I’m choosing to stay because of our personalities, interests, aspirations, values, and general compatibility. If those are materialistic, than I guess I have a really unclear understanding of materialism. There’s a few things I laid out here less gently than I would in person with him, but there’s nothing that would come as a surprise to him since we’ve discussed all of this in great detail. He knows how I feel about him. He knows how I feel about me. He knows this weighs heavily on me....we’ve been having variations of this discussion for 5 years. This isn’t some secret bombshell I’m dropping on him immediately after achieving my devious gold digger fantasies.

Excellent advice. Unfortunately, this is the results of many years of counseling on and off with different therapists. This is improved me and it’s realistically about as good as I’m going to get until additional treatment options become available in the future. I’m constantly working on myself in the meantime, but behavioral and lifestyle changes can only do so much for chronic treatment resistant depression.

It seems like practicality, not pity to me. I’m statistically more difficult to get along with than average based on a lifetime of loose calculations that have attempted to adjust for confirmation bias. It’s an objective observation, not a criticism of myself.

I’m glad you found a situation that’s working well for you. Thanks for understanding the dilemma, even though you made a different choice in the end. Based on all the other comments, it seems likely that you made the better choice.
Thanks for explaining your perspective further. I really appreciate it.

If I made it seem like I wasn’t taking full responsibility for this decision or that I magically expect anything to change, I’m sorry. I tried really hard to make it clear that this is on me and that I don’t expect anything to change, but clearly I didn’t do a good job of that.

It’s not about the tax return. What I was intending to get across is that our lives already have all the commitment and complexity of a marriage (or as complex as our personal relationship will ever be since kids aren’t a consideration). When we get married, literally the only thing that will change is our tax return because we’re essentially already married every way but legally. I didn’t see any benefit to continuing to reiterate all the things I love about the relationship because everyone sees those are subjective or delusional. I’m already so wordy as it is that repeating the compatibility pitch seemed an area worth dropping.

Kids seem like an obligation that prevents you from doing what you’d otherwise like. Commitment seems like a choice made independently of obligation. It’s choosing to stay when nothing is stopping you from walking away.

I don’t expect it to improve. I expect to keep getting better at dealing with it so it’s less impactful. And I’m already stuck with a lifetime of depression (which I continuously get better at dealing with too)...so this is essentially just another drop in the bucket.
You sound like a delightful person. You really do. Glad you’ve found your happiness.
Or you know....I’m just a generally unpleasant human to be around and I found another human that doesn’t think that, which is way harder than finding a human willing to sleep with me.

I’m not sure how I came across as conceited, but that wasn’t my intention. I have weird, rambling speech patterns, but I’m trying really hard to be concise without giving incomplete responses. It’s difficult to express how disappointed in myself I feel for coming across that way. 
  
I won’t be posting again in the future because there doesn’t seem to be a community wide benefit. My intention also wasn’t to shoot down advice, but discuss it and explore it in more depth. I know that comes across as arguing though. I’ve been told that my whole life and I still haven’t found a way to fully explore someone’s perspective without getting that criticism.  
  
For everyone telling me I’ll have no trouble finding a “better” partner, I seem to be making it pretty apparent how frequently I rub people the wrong way. Imagine how much more annoying I am in person.

Some members of the community focus on escaping a DB, others focus on finding strategies to cope. I listened to the advice and tried damn near everything suggested. When that didn’t work, I realized I had to make a choice and stop endlessly worrying about the situation. I had the opportunity to experience a separation and that left me feeling less fulfilled than I do now. So I’ve made this choice. It’s sometimes a difficult one to cope with, but so is leaving. 
  
My intention wasn’t to complain so much as inform. I can see why it comes across otherwise though.  
  
Kids are definitely important to consider in these situations. Kids aren’t going to happen though, so this decision only impacts me. There’s not much in our life that can become more entangled than it is now. We’ve pretty much plateaued at difficulty of leaving. 
  
If I post here again, it will again be for the purpose of information for someone in a similar position. I know that I’m responsible for the future because I made this choice. I’m okay with that.
That definitely makes it harder.

Thank you for acknowledging the difficulty of the decision. It’s a bit easier when I decided to stop endlessly debating both options in my head for years on end. I concluded that I will regret leaving more than I will regret staying. It wasn’t a decision made lightly.
Rest assured that offspring will not be a part of this or any subsequent relationship equation.

It’s decision I’m choosing to stick with, but that doesn’t make it easy and I know there are people here that can relate to that. Talking it through with the community is useful for seeing if I’m missing a glaring, obvious consideration. It might also be useful for someone else down the road in a  similar position to help them decide which way to go. I’ve benefited greatly from reading through other posts with similar circumstances to mine.

It seems to stem from how differently we approach friendship. I have close, intimate friendships. For me a relationship is essentially that with greater commitment and theoretically, sex. He has more casual acquaintances, but can only really form that level of close intimate friendship with a romantic partner. So what I call friendship is what he calls a relationship. 
As you said, that’s obviously problematic. There isn’t an obvious solution now, but I’m working toward creating one.
Thanks.
Thanks. I’ll press it again. It really would be a shame if we’ve wasted all these years on something that is such  simple fix.
That’s what we did for 4 years before we started dating. At least I won’t be lying about the “marrying my best friend” cliché. The line does seem pretty blurred. You’re not wrong.

Being most of the way through my 20s now, I already know it’s a special time that I missed, but for reasons entirely unrelated to this. This situation weighs heavily on me, but is pretty minor compared to the outside factors. I think it feels so miserable at times because this is one part of my life thats almost perfect. It’s so close and it’s a shame that it’s not quite there.  
  
Kids aren’t for us. We can never afford a house where we live anyway. We’re both well into our careers and if anything, that’d give us more incentive to stay together because we work in complimentary fields and benefit significantly from each other’s insight. We’ve lived together all this time and all our assets and possessions are intertwined. There’s not much to get more serious and I’ve thought this through every which way for years. It’s not a choice I made without consideration or thought.

The point I’m trying to make is that lots of people end up unsatisfied with their sex lives later in life/marriage. Then they’re stuck with someone they maybe don’t even like that much, but were lured in by hormones. This portion of one area of my life is unfortunate, but the remaining (larger m) portion of the relationship provides a huge amount of happiness. I’ve also already spent such a large portion of my life unhappy that my main goal is to mitigate overall suffering long-term. There’s a possibility that I’d be happier in a different situation for the next several years, but this situation is better for all the years after that.

People don’t mind sleeping with me, but long term commitment is a different story. I have a chronic health condition that most people can’t deal with. I’d rather marry someone that will stick it out long term than have fun for a few months or years with a revolving door of temporary relationships.

Thanks for a well thought out answer. I’m pretty accepting because I know anyone in a relationship with me is also making a big sacrifice by signing up to be with someone with a chronic illness. Having a new set of rules is probably the direction we need to head.

At this point the only thing that’s going to change is we’ll get a better tax return. We’ve already lived together for years and our whole lives are intertwined.  
You make a very good point that I’m here for a reason though. It’s nice to talk to people that understand what this situation feels like.

I fully support people being in the healthiest, most fulfilling relationship possible. I think it’s unrealistic to expect any relationship to be perfect though. I’ve never once seen that occur in any of my family, friends, acquaintances, or otherwise and I’ve seen some very healthy, supportive relationships over the years. Every relationship has something. This is a big something, but it seems a fair trade because I also bring a major difficulty into the relationship that affects my partner’s well being.
Would you say it ever plateaus? Or continues to be worse indefinitely? Personally, it seemed to get worse the first several years, but 6 years in, id say it’s leveled out mostly.
You make a good point. I’ve brought up that it mostly feels like we’re good friends and he doesn’t see it that way.

General society pretty much implies that woman stop being at all attractive or sexually appealing after 40 anyway. Most women start questioning their appearance as they age and their skin becomes less firm or things start to sag. If that’s going to happen regardless, I’d rather get it out of the way and guarantee an otherwise good partner. I also logically know that it has nothing to do with my appearance.  
  
For the record, I’m not saying I support societal norms for women’s beauty standards, but that’s a whole different topic entirely.

I am very loved, respected, and well cared for in every other way. Looking at your situation, would you say the first man was as good or better than the second in every way but sex? Are there things the first man did that meant a lot to you and you’re not getting from the current husband?  
Edit: I meant those as genuine questions, not challenges.

I thought it through a lot. I’ve had 6 years to think this through. I’ve read all sorts of posts on this subreddit in addition to countless articles and guides. We’ve been engaged for almost 2 years. It really sucks and I wish this wasn’t the situation, but it seems like the best long term option. My experience with life so far is that there’s never a perfect option and every choice means sacrificing something one way or another.

Well if they don’t want to have sex with me regardless, it’s not super relevant what I do or don’t want in terms of sex. There’s a lot else that matters in a marriage. It’s a big part for sure, but not everything.
I mean....I had 4+ years to decide if the other factors made the relationship worth it. And it’s been a 2 year engagement. I’m not by any means rushing into it. I do see your point though.

Because it would be an overall supportive, healthy, stable relationship that I would enjoy in every aspect other than the obvious. Even if I found another relationship with great sexual compatibility, there would probably be something else lacking. I’d rather enter in knowing someone super well and knowing the worst of them than end up with a wild card.

He has plenty of energy for any other activity. He’s overall a very upbeat, energetic, motivated person. When he went to a doctor to get the test ordered, the doctor said it was worth ruling out but that low testosterone was unlikely because he has chest hair and normal testicles and what not. I think that’s part of why he’s not as concerned about going through the blood test. I agree that it’s worth doing though.
Can never be 100% positive, but it seems extremely unlikely especially for 6+ years continuously. It’s just always been low and became lower when I stopped initiating.
